fine_trace.code: blosc2_schunk* schunk = blosc2_schunk_from_buffer((uint8_t *) data, size, false);
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are parsed as an in-memory contiguous frame; copy=false means frame->cframe points directly into the input buffer.
The frame's cframe pointer aliases the fuzzer input buffer; no copy is made, so any free() on a pointer derived from cframe is invalid.
With copy=false, frame_to_schunk skips chunk validation and returns a schunk whose nchunks is derived solely from the frame header (nbytes/chunksize).

fine_trace.note: The fuzzer iterates over chunks; a crafted header with nbytes/chunksize >= 2 causes at least one decompress_chunk call.

Calls frame_get_lazychunk to obtain the chunk pointer; the returned rc is the lazychunk cbytes.
Reads the chunk offset from the compressed offsets chunk; a crafted offsets chunk yields an offset pointing to invalid chunk data.
For in-memory frames, *chunk is set to a pointer into the input buffer (frame->cframe + header_len + offset), not a heap allocation.
Validates the chunk header at the offset; a crafted offset pointing to invalid header bytes makes blosc2_cbuffer_sizes return a negative rc.
